problem: Prior long-horizon/lifelong navigation methods retain scene knowledge (graphs, snapshots, memories) or train retrieval policies, but do not let a general multi-round reasoning session consult, compare and revise spatial memory, task records and house knowledge across fresh sessions. Independent per-task sessions discard experience, and a single long session accumulates stale context.
motivation: A household robot handles successive requests where each task starts where the last ended, so accumulated maps and search evidence should help. But records like 'not found in room' do not prove full inspection and may conflict with current views, so the navigator must interpret and revise them against observations, and wrong completion claims can pollute later experience.
key_idea: An embodied harness where fresh multi-round agentic sessions read and write external memory (map, task handovers, ledger, house notes), with structured recovery handovers, judge-based completion checks and run-end consolidation, all without extra model training.
insight: How experience is used matters beyond retaining it. Ablations on Opus 5 show a single long session (54.9) is worse than independent sessions (58.9), removing cross-task memory costs 14.7 s-SR, and a structured recovery handover beats a matched-length summary by 8.3 points, an empty handover barely helps (72.9 vs 71.1 without recovery) and another task's note hurts (68.5). Consolidation adds 7.7 s-SR on 10-tour deployments beyond maps and task records.
method: Orchestrator: outer loop that manages fresh sessions per task/recovery, advances sessions in hops, tracks turn (200) and movement (500) budgets shared across attempts, and writes ledger and verdict files

Three-tier memory: active context, working memory (SLAM occupancy maps, named markers with photos, ledger, task handovers, recovery notes), and long-term house notes (index, overview, room notes, skills) read via file tools
Tool interface: observe, step (0.25 m / 15° / STOP), get_map, mark, preview_path (A* on known free cells), read/write/list files, request_recovery, close_task; ORB-SLAM3 RGB-D poses feed the mapper

Recovery with structured handover: a fresh conversation starts after the outgoing session writes a recovery note (searched vs ruled-out with supporting evidence, untried options); scoped reassessment (attempt/place/room/floor/house) and a wake-up session that relocalizes from saved photos

Judge session verification: tool-free judge sees goal, four stop views, sampled frames, map and records and returns complete/incomplete/unknown; pre-stop verification can veto the first stop once, and post-stop certification only labels the record

Consolidation session: at run end, rewrites the four house-note files from the journal and old notes, adding skills only when journal-supported, separating checked outcomes from claims, with write access restricted to those files

setting.backbone: Frozen reasoning cores in a coding-agent harness: Qwen3.8-27B, GPT-4o, Opus 5, GPT-6 Astra (also used as judge/consolidation/wake-up sessions)
setting.model_size: Qwen3.8-27B is the only open model; others are proprietary
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with SLAM-estimated pose (ORB-SLAM3), forward RGB view via observe tool
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT/RIGHT 15° / STOP
setting.privileged: none (no simulator GT pose, no global navmesh, no auxiliary perception models); benchmark runs start with empty memory per episode/tour

numbers_note: IR2R-CE is mapped to R2R-CE as the closest canonical name but is the lifelong/tour variant with s-SR/e-SR/t-nDTW metrics. Ablation and deployment numbers (e.g., 80.5 s-SR with consolidation vs 72.8 without) are not listed as benchmark rows.
results: With SLAM poses instead of GT poses, NavHarness (GPT-6 Astra) reaches 83.7 s-SR / 62.3 SPL / 36.9 e-SR on GOAT-Bench, beating the strongest prior HIMM (72.8 s-SR) and AstraNav-Memory (56.9 SPL), and 85.9 s-SR on IR2R-CE vs SeqWalker's 36. It improves s-SR over same-backbone independent sessions by 18.6 to 34.8 points across all four backbones.
limitations: Memory reliability: an incorrect completion accepted by the judge can propagate into house notes, and correcting one record does not update copies or validate other spatial claims

Gains are measured against context-only independent-session controls, and the full harness bundles mapping, recovery and verification, so it is not a pure memory comparison against prior methods; evaluation only in simulation with frontier proprietary models
Benchmark runs start each episode/tour with empty memory, so cross-run consolidation is only evaluated in a separate concatenated-deployment study
